current_example.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following multiplication problem:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/8889a8caf91247de656b139eac0ac1cda307a95304fa3f31c6b66b3b43b4c7ac.svg)

Notice that the first fraction's denominator (![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/b992f271508479b55a84d515f24ad943e6d6cebee3cf8ca8eba23c53d2ffce30.svg)) and the second fraction's numerator (![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/e6c919a9391008f140a302a91592baadf4fda7df09436f355d97029a17a0452a.svg)) have a common 
factor of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/fe34f715005da1a8b682c9650a76785673fdf25c3b7c7546bb94824470c54caf.svg) 

Therefore, we can simplify our problem by first swapping the denominators:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/01248649d0990953974a79f89b48a1cc95c30f9a5d0614b31c38bacefec9f639.svg)

Next, we reduce the second fraction to its lowest terms by dividing the numerator and denominator by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/fe34f715005da1a8b682c9650a76785673fdf25c3b7c7546bb94824470c54caf.svg) 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/15c1044aca3df2ff8f02df2e860fefb8d7f640f9bfa333b16bb44d4689aa7361.svg)

To multiply two fractions, we multiply the numerators and we multiply the denominators:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131633/assets/7bb4e93fe78704795ace2ead756ff9fc49da5fd9ec1479f2b44e823e37e1be6f.svg)
